what_it_does: splits a BeautifulSoup page into markdown sections, growing each section's text line by line with string concatenation

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C10.S4 — `text = text + "\n" + line` (line 97) copies the accumulated section on every markdown line; collecting the lines and joining once per section gives the same text (the `if text:` flush becomes a test on the collected parts)

what_it_does: returns the language name for a code block by calling get_text() on it and testing a few substrings

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: el.text (a get_text() walk of the code block's descendants) is evaluated up to three times for one element; binding it once removes the two repeat walks on every path that reaches the later checks

what_it_does: returns the string with every Unicode control/format character removed, one character at a time

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C10.S1 — a per-character generator calls unicodedata.category for every character of every chunk (line 7); a str.translate table built once does the same filtering in C

what_it_does: returns True when a noun phrase starts with one of eight stop prefixes

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C10.S3 — `for f in invalid_starts: if text.startswith(f)` makes one call per prefix (lines 68-70); a single startswith with a tuple of the prefixes answers the same question in one call

what_it_does: returns True when a candidate title is too short or long, or contains a banned character

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C4.S2 — `len(text) < 3` already returned True on line 58, so `text.startswith("/") and len(text) < 3` (line 60) can never be true; deleting it removes a startswith call per title that gets this far (report-only, one call per input)

what_it_does: reads product metadata, converts it and writes it as indented JSON to the output file

decisions.label: a

what_it_does: reads reviews, converts them and writes them as indented JSON to the output file

what_it_does: counts term occurrences across documents and sums the per-term document counts

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `total_count = sum([...])` at line 92 is bound and never read, so each document's counts are summed for nothing (card C1.S1 pattern 1)

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: C3.S4 — for each unique term, `sum([1 if term in doc for doc in doc_counts])` (lines 100-103) scans every document, O(terms x docs); the per-document term sets are already in hand in the first pass, so the document count can be taken there (inner level is a search over the docs list)

what_it_does: builds the feed list of term documents and writes it as indented JSON to a file

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C10.S2 — re.sub(r" ", "/", term) (line 27) runs a literal one-character replacement through the regex engine per term; term.replace(" ", "/") gives the same string (card C10.S2 pattern 1)

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: C9.S1 — json.dump writes the encoder's chunks one fp.write at a time (lines 38-39); json.dumps builds the same text (same indent, same bytes) and one write puts it in the file. The pure-Python encoder is used either way, so the saving is the many calls, not the encoder

what_it_does: counts all n-gram windows of a token list that contain no common word

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C10.S1 — `not any(map(lambda word: word in common_words, window))` (lines 59-61) runs a Python lambda per word per window; `not common_words.isdisjoint(window)` is one C-level call with the same answer

what_it_does: collects the set of distinct words from the titles and contents of all documents

decisions.why: C10.S3 — term_set.add(term) is called per term in two loops (lines 28-32); term_set.update(clean_text(...)) does each loop's work in one call (report: a set update per document)

The list's len() is still used on line 72, so the repair keeps the list and adds a set beside it

what_it_does: returns the set of document ids for the sampled queries plus random extra documents

decisions.label: b

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: C8.S2 — BertTokenizer.from_pretrained and BertModel.from_pretrained (lines 47-48) rebuild the model on every call, and main calls create_embeddings twice (lines 77-78); the artefacts never change, so loading them once per process is the repair (blocked: needs the Hugging Face weights)

decisions.label: c

decisions.label: d

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `Looks like it, but is not`: the duplicate `embed(@query)` is two request keys the profile reads (`embedding` for the binary tensor and `float_embedding` for the float one); the repeat is a server-side call the request contract needs, not a repeated computation in this function

what_it_does: builds the Vespa query body for the second phase of feature collection

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: same as first phase: `embedding` and `float_embedding` are both inputs the profile reads, so removing one changes the request contract

what_it_does: builds the Vespa query body for the first ranking phase

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: same contract reason: the two embed inputs are both read by the ranking profile; the f-string built twice is the only client-side repeat and it is negligible

what_it_does: builds the Vespa query body for the second ranking phase

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: same contract reason as rank_first_phase_query_fn

what_it_does: builds the Vespa query body for the weakAnd match-only evaluation

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C1.S5 — the request sends input.query(embedding) (an embed call server-side) that the match-only profile never reads; removing the key drops a computation nothing consumes (needs Vespa to show it)

what_it_does: trains LightGBM over cross-validation folds, renames features, and writes the model

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C3.S4 — for each selected feature a linear scan over feature_name_mapping.items() (lines 249, 254) finds the renamed column; a reverse dict answers each in O(1). Feature counts are small, so the saving is small

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: C5.S4 — the model dict is dumped to a string, each feature name is regex-substituted across the whole JSON (one pass per feature), then re-parsed and dumped again; renaming the dict directly avoids the serialise/parse round trip

what_it_does: prints feature statistics, runs five-fold logistic regression, and writes the coefficients

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `X[feature].describe()` runs for every feature (line 103) and computes count and quartiles (a sort per column) that are never read; only mean, std, min and max are printed (C1.S5 pattern 1)

what_it_does: loads the images, builds the similarity tensor, and yields one blended heatmap per image and token

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `processed_images` is appended at line 88 and read nowhere; the list and its appends go, the loop and `img_pil` stay (C1.S1 pattern 2, a loop filling a list nothing reads) — report-only, the saving is one append per image

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: C6.S2 — `img_pil.copy()` (line 86) makes a full-size copy of every image; _blend_image never mutates its img argument and does not read it, so the copy buys nothing (blocked: needs a ColPali instance)

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: C3.S2 — should_filter_token(token) depends only on the token and is re-run for every image (line 99); hoisting the filter out of the image loop keeps the yield order (pattern 3)

what_it_does: fills a patch-by-token tensor from the Vespa similarity cells

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C3.S2 — the hasattr test and image_seq_length (lines 147-150) depend only on self.processor, which never changes, yet are recomputed for every cell in the innermost loop

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `Looks like it, but is not`: the scalar item assignments write in loop order, so when two cells map to the same (image, token, row, col) the last one wins; index_put with duplicate indices does not promise that order, so the batched form can change values

what_it_does: returns True for tokens that are special, whitespace, punctuation, or underscore-prefixed

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C8.S2 — re.compile(...) (line 253) builds the same pattern per call; the repair compiles it once, e.g. as a default argument evaluated at definition time, so the signature still takes just the token (card: the re cache makes the repeat cheap, so expect a small saving)

what_it_does: logs a one-line summary of a Vespa response and returns its JSON

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `result_text` is passed to logger.debug, so it is logged output under the contract; it is not resultless (C1.S5 near-miss: a value consumed by logging)

what_it_does: runs the ColPali or hybrid query for a ranking and returns the formatted results

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C1.S3 pattern 1 — the colpali and hybrid arms make the identical query_vespa_colpali call, so the test that picks between them changes nothing that runs (report-only: one comparison per query)

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `Looks like it, but is not`: the loop calls logger.debug for each child; those debug lines are logged output under the same-logged-output contract, so the loop is not resultless

what_it_does: converts the query embedding to float and binary forms and sends the ColPali nearest-neighbour query to Vespa

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C5.S4 — the query tensor goes tensor -> tolist() (format_q_embs) -> np.array -> packbits for the binary query; the sign bits could come from the tensor. Report-only: the float list is still needed for input.query(qt), so the saving is one array conversion per query, and the repair spans float_to_binary_embedding

what_it_does: queries Vespa for questions matching a prefix and returns the distinct ones

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C10.S1 — set([item for sublist in questions for item in sublist]) (line 364) is a hand-written flatten where set().union(*questions) does the same in C (blocked: the unit calls Vespa)

what_it_does: runs the ColPali model over the images and returns one embedding array

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C10.S3 — batch_size (line 534) is never passed to DataLoader (line 555), so the default batch of one gives one model forward per page; passing it batches the forward (blocked: needs the ColPali model)

what_it_does: converts each float query vector to packed binary form

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C10.S1 — a Python loop calls np.array, np.where, np.packbits and tolist once per patch vector (lines 587-591); one vectorised packbits over the stacked array does the same work

what_it_does: decodes a base64 image and saves it to a file

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the re-encoded file is the output: writing the raw bytes changes the stored file whenever the source is not already the encoding PIL writes, so it is not resultless

what_it_does: queries the similarity maps, waits for the images, and writes one PNG per image and token

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C8.S1 — every search re-runs the Vespa _sim query and rewrites every blended PNG (lines 262-294), though the files are named by query_id and the output is deterministic per (query, ranking); skipping existing files needs an invalidation rule (blocked: needs Vespa and ColPali)

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: C6.S3 — `all([os.path.exists(...) for ...])` (lines 273-277) builds the full list of stat results on every 0.2 s poll; `all(...)` over a generator stops at the first missing file (pattern 3). Report-only, the list is short

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: C4.S2 — after the while loop, `if not all([...])` (line 278) re-stats every image even when the loop already exited because they all existed; a flag set in the loop settles the answer (report-only; blocked: needs Vespa and ColPali)

what_it_does: route handler ('/fetch_results') that computes the ColPali query embeddings for the query and runs the search

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C11.S4 — the synchronous ColPali query embedding runs inside an async def (lines 205-207), holding the event loop for the forward pass (blocked: needs the ColPali model)

what_it_does: route handler that returns query suggestions from Vespa for a prefix

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C8.S1 — each request runs an uncached Vespa regex query for the same prefix (lines 349-354); the repair caches suggestions per prefix with a stated lifetime (blocked: needs Vespa)

what_it_does: streams the Gemini answer as server-sent events after waiting for the result images

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: C3.S3 — Image.open(image_filename) re-runs for every ready document on every 0.2 s poll (lines 369-380), reopening images opened on the previous pass; caching the opened images would keep them across polls (blocked by the Gemini/web path)

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: C7.S5 — `min(num_images, len(doc_ids))` in the while condition (line 365) equals num_images, since num_images = min(3, len(doc_ids)) (line 360); the expression is the same value every poll (report-only)

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: `Looks like it, but is not`: response_text is yielded in full on every chunk (line 404), so it is read on each pass; the deferred join the card describes would send empty or stale text

decisions.label: d
decisions.why: C1.S5 — six f-string log messages are formatted on each idx and each poll and discarded at INFO level (report-only; lazy formatting keeps the DEBUG text)

what_it_does: embeds each image of a split with the model and feeds the documents to Vespa in batches

decisions.label: a

The repair must not count non-image rows as skipped (the original does not count them), so the skip test goes first and the image test keeps its own branch

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: C1.S4 — abs_path.exists() is evaluated at line 140 and again at line 144 for the same file; one stat serves both (report-only; blocked: needs the model and Vespa)

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: C8.S4 — abs_path.read_bytes() (line 152) reads the JPEG and then Image.open(abs_path) (line 153) re-reads and decodes the same file; decoding from BytesIO(jpeg_bytes) keeps one read (blocked: needs the model and Vespa)
